resale_co.name: Residential Resale Certificate (Certificate of Continued Occupancy, CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Building Department (Construction Code Official; Housing Inspector schedules re-inspections)
resale_co.lead_time: Request at least 10 business days before the inspection date; the certificate is issued 2 full business days after final approval
resale_co.valid_for: 3 months from the date of issue, unless occupancy or ownership changes in the meantime; not transferable
requirements: Smoke detectors on each level and within 10 feet of each separate sleeping area; battery alarms must be 10-year sealed units since January 1, 2019
Two-family homes also need a smoke detector at the highest level of each common stairwell
Existing hardwired smoke and CO systems must be kept to the level of the original certificate of occupancy; battery alarms are not acceptable replacements
No double-sided tape for mounting detectors
CO alarms outside each sleeping area, within 10 feet of bedroom doors
Portable fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen area: at least 2A:10B:C, no larger than 10 lbs, on a hanger or bracket, top no more than 5 feet above the floor, visible, near an exit path
All open permits closed out with the proper inspections
Sheds, fences, pools, decks and garages must have permits on file for the CCO application to be accepted
Owner certifies the property meets zoning and that no rubbish, debris or bulk garbage will be left before the new occupancy

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online with the Township's GovPilot 'Certificate of Continued Occupancy Application' (choose Resale), enter the closing date and contact for the inspection, and pay the $175.00 fee by debit or credit card. Inspections are Monday to Friday between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.; the owner or a representative must be home. For a re-inspection, call the office (do not re-apply) and a payment link for $80.00 will be emailed.

evidence.quote: Procedure for Obtaining Residential Resale Certificate
Certificate requests must be made a minimum of ten (10) business days in advance of the inspection date.
A certificate of continued occupancy will not be issued unless the inspection fee is paid.
The purpose of this inspection is to verify locations of smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors & fire extinguishers.
The certificate will remain valid for a three (3) months from the date of issue unless the occupancy or ownership of the dwelling changes in the interim.
The certificate will be issued two (2) full business days after final approval.
For reinspection, call office & s link will be sent. Fee is $80 each.
Certificate of Continued Occupancy fee: ... $175.00 ... $80.00 per re-inspection ... Payable by debit or credit card only.

All of the structures below require permits before they can be installed at the property. If the structure exists already then a permit must be established in order for your CCO application to be accepted.

resale_co.notes: The Building Department's 'Procedure for Obtaining Residential Resale Certificate' (PDF created November 8, 2024) and the GovPilot application both show $175.00 plus $80.00 per re-inspection. The Township Code (ecode360, which could not be opened) was found by an exact-words web search for 'certificate of continued occupancy has been issued by the Construction Code Official of the Township of Union' (section amended 8-23-2022 by Ord. No. 5739); search results also describe 'A fee of $50 shall be charged and paid to the Township for each original certificate of continued occupancy', which does not match the posted $175.00, so the town is on the call sheet. Building Department email building@uniontownship.com is a mailto link on the Township directory. Office hours: Mon/Tues/Thurs/Fri 8:30 to 4:30pm. Rental registration is a separate program; 3-or-more-family homes also need a State green card.

requirements: Battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units (since January 1, 2019)
Two-family homes need a smoke detector at the highest level of each common stairwell
Hardwired smoke and CO systems must be maintained as originally approved; no battery replacements
Portable fire extinguisher still required on the Township's 2024 sheet: at least 2A:10B:C, no more than 10 lbs, within 10 feet of the kitchen, mounted with the top no more than 5 feet above the floor

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA July 2026 registry lists the Township of Union Fire Department as the fire code enforcing agency. The Township's own resale procedure puts the smoke, CO and extinguisher check into the Building Department's Residential Resale Certificate (CCO) inspection, so that office and fee are listed. The state fire directory instead lists 'Union Twp Fire Prev' for smoke detector compliance (phone (908) 851-5437) and Fire Official Orland Guzman ((908) 851-5422, oguzman@uniontownship.com). The Fire Prevention Bureau page lists Fire Prevention at 908.851.5434 and Fire Director Raul Malave III (fire@uniontownship.com). If a buyer's lender or attorney asks for a separate fire certificate, confirm with the Fire Prevention Bureau.

other_items.label: Open permits closed
other_items.detail: All open permits must be closed out with the proper inspections before the resale inspection; existing sheds, fences, pools, decks and garages need permits on file.

other_items.label: No debris left
other_items.detail: The owner certifies no rubbish, debris or bulk garbage will be left on the property before new occupancy; otherwise the CCO can be retracted and a summons issued.
